design_rationale: Patients were randomly allocated using a computer-generated randomization code (1:1:2) with sealed envelopes prepared by the quality of care unit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was computer-generated with allocation concealed via envelopes prepared by an independent unit, and baseline characteristics were balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomization code was generated by a computer 1:1:2 and envelopes with allocation were prepared by the quality of care unit. A nurse from the Nephrology Unit opened the envelopes and prepared the syringes for injection. Investigators and patients were blinded to the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind design with identical single intravenous injections prepared by a dedicated nurse, with no reported deviations from assigned interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Investigators and patients were blinded to the treatment. Randomized injection occurred on arrival to the intensive care unit between 1 and 4 hours after surgery... Patients and care-takers were blinded for the assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for virtually all participants (79 of 80 with complete biological follow-up and clinical status known for all 80).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No patient was excluded after randomization... Only 1 patient was transferred in another hospital at 48 h. Although we could not have the complete biological follow-up, we could have the information that he did not develop AKI and was alive.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory biomarkers and clinical definitions measured using standardized assays by blinded personnel.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Rapid NGAL ELISA kit (Bioport Diagnostics-Gentofte, Denmark) was used to measure urinary NGAL (uNGAL)... All samples for NGAL and cytokines measures were processed at the same time.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was pre-registered (NCT00676234) and reported the pre-specified primary outcome and secondary outcomes according to the planned analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the ethical committee from Geneva University Hospital and registered at ClinicalTrial.gov (NCT00676234). The primary outcome was the change in urinary NGAL concentration from baseline and 48 h after r-HuEPO injection.

overall_summary: The trial was well-conducted with computer-generated randomization, allocation concealment, double-blinding, minimal missing data, objective laboratory outcomes, and pre-registration with consistent reporting. All domains were judged to have a low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to either the rHuEPO or placebo group using blocked randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study used blocked randomization with allocation concealment via sealed envelopes opened by non-participating nurses, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment assignment among the two groups was determined by blocked randomization. After recruitment, three days before the operation, sealed envelopes containing the allocation group were opened by nurses who did not participate in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients, care providers, and investigators were blinded using identical syringes and saline placebo, minimizing deviations from intended interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pairs of identical 0.3 ml syringes containing either rHuEPO (5,000 U, Recormon, Roche) or saline were prepared and stored... Patients and investigators were also blinded to group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were complete for all 100 patients who received the intervention, with only two pre-surgery cancellations evenly distributed between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One patient in the rHuEPO and one from the placebo group were excluded because of the lack of medical treatment and a CABG cancelation. Consequently, 100 patients received their assigned treatments to the placebo (n = 50) or rHuEPO (n = 50) group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory-based measurements (serum creatinine, eGFR, urine NGAL) performed using standard methods in a blinded fashion.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All laboratory parameters were performed in a single, hospital-based laboratory using standard methods... The measurements were made in duplicate and in a blinded fashion.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01066351) and reported prespecified primary and secondary endpoints in accordance with standard diagnostic definitions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint of this study was the incidence of CSA-AKI in rHuEPO compared with placebo group... Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01066351

overall_summary: The study is a well-conducted double-blind randomized controlled trial with adequate sequence generation, allocation concealment, complete follow-up, and objective, blinded outcome assessment, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with participants allocated to treatment groups via an electronic web-based randomization system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Centralized web-based randomization with stratification was used, ensuring sequence generation and allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization to study treatment was performed by authorized secretaries via an Internet homepage (at the Department of Clinical Epidemiology, Aarhus University, Denmark) and was stratified by sex, age (above or below 70 years), center and cancer localization (colon or rectum). Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study personnel were blinded using matched placebo packaging and administration protocols, with no reported protocol deviations affecting intervention delivery.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was designed as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study... Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times. Code-breaking sheets for emergency use were available but were never used.

domain_judgments.rationale: About 25% of randomized participants (51/202) were excluded from the analysis post-randomization (due to post-randomization criteria, dropouts, and deaths), and analyses were restricted to an efficacy-valid population rather than full intention-to-treat imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 221 patients were enrolled into the study, of whom 202 patients were randomized and 151 completed the study (efficacy-valid population).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors and participants were blinded, and outcomes were evaluated using standardized, objective instruments across both arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times... Changes in patients’ work capacity were assessed using a cycle ergometer test (Ergoline Ergometrics 900; Kivex A/S, Horsholm, Denmark).

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses followed a pre-established analysis plan with predefined primary and secondary endpoints, and all outcomes were reported as specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure were the changes in patients’ physical performance from preoperative to postoperative day 7... Data were entered before treatment codes were broken and analyzed on an intent-to-treat basis according to a preestablished analysis plan.

overall_summary: The study was a well-designed, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial, but carries some concerns overall due to missing outcome data resulting from the post-randomization exclusion of approximately 25% of randomized participants.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 using a computer-generated block randomization list stratified by baseline serum creatinine and cardiopulmonary bypass use.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central web-based allocation was used with computer-generated sequence and baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomization code list with a block size of two was generated by Medical Research Collaborating Center Seoul National University Hospital. The randomization was stratified on the basis of SCr ( ! 1.5 and 6 1.5 mg/dl) and use of CPB during surgery. Treatments were allocated to patients through the Internet in accordance with the predefined randomization list (1:1 ratio for EPO or placebo group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind placebo-controlled design with single-dose preoperative administration given under anesthesia ensured blinding of participants and caregivers and adherence to protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients, healthcare clinicians, and investigators were blinded to treatment assignment. A 2-ml syringe containing either EPO (Recormon, Roche) or placebo was prepared. Each of the syringes contained either 300 U/kg of EPO or the same volume of normal saline corresponding to the dose of EPO.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 71 randomized patients completed the trial and were included in the primary outcome analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 71 patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 36) or saline (n = 35) and completed this trial. Figure 1 depicts patient flow through the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Acute kidney injury and renal function were assessed using objective laboratory measurements of serum creatinine with assessors and investigators blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the incidence of AKI after CABG, defined as a 50% increase in SCr levels from baseline at any time within the first 5 postoperative days... SCr was measured using modified Jaffé method on a Toshiba 200FR Analyzer (Toshiba, Tokyo, Japan).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, and the predefined primary and secondary endpoints are reported as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (www.clinicaltrial.gov), No. NCT 00654992. The primary endpoint was the incidence of AKI after CABG, defined as a 50% increase in SCr levels from baseline at any time within the first 5 postoperative days.

overall_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial has low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains, with robust central allocation concealment, double blinding, complete follow-up, and objective laboratory outcome measurement.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sequence generation was computer-generated, allocation was performed by a ward physician not involved in the trial, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly allocated to either the rHuEPO or the control group in a 1:1 ratio by means of computer-generated random numbers. A ward physician not involved in the current trial performed randomization and assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgeons and anesthesiologists managing the patients were blinded to group assignment, transfusion decisions were protocol-driven by predefined hemoglobin thresholds, and an intention-to-treat approach was used with no reported deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Medications were prepared and administered by a ward physician recognizing the patient’s group but not involved in the current study, whereas the surgeon and anesthesiologist involved in the study and patient management were blinded to the patients’ groups until the end of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were complete for all 74 randomized participants with no missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: VHS could be performed as planned in all patients, and complete data sets from the 74 patients were analyzed without any missing data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Transfusion requirements and laboratory outcomes were objectively measured according to explicit protocol thresholds by blinded clinical teams.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hemoglobin concentration less than 7 mg/dl during CPB, and less than 8 mg/dl after CPB and postoperatively, were used as transfusion thresholds... the surgeon and anesthesiologist involved in the study and patient management were blinded to the patients’ groups until the end of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Reported results align directly with the prespecified primary and secondary outcomes and statistical analysis plan detailed in the methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was transfusion requirement assessed during the surgery and for 4 days postoperatively. Reticulocyte count and iron profiles were measured serially and compared preoperatively and on postoperative days 1, 2, 4, and 7.

overall_summary: The trial demonstrated robust randomization and allocation concealment, adequate blinding of clinical care providers and outcome assessors, no missing outcome data, objective protocol-driven transfusion criteria, and consistent reporting of prespecified endpoints.

design_rationale: The study is a pre-planned secondary analysis of the EPO-TBI trial, an international multicenter randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated to either erythropoietin or saline placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The underlying EPO-TBI study was a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with central web-based randomization and concealed allocation, and no notable baseline imbalances suggesting failure of randomization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The EPO-TBI study was an international randomized controlled trial... Enrolled patients received either weekly doses of 40 000 IU of subcutaneous epoetin alfa... or placebo (0.9% sodium chloride). The randomization process and administration of drug has been described previously.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was blinded using an identical placebo (0.9% sodium chloride) and analysed according to intention-to-treat principles with minimal post-randomization protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The EPO-TBI sub-study was a pre-planned study and the protocol (a part of the original EPO-AKI protocol) is included in the Supplementary Materials... Enrolled patients received either weekly doses of 40 000 IU of subcutaneous epoetin alfa... or placebo (0.9% sodium chloride).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 603 of 606 randomized patients (>99.5%), with only 3 patients excluded due to consent withdrawal, indicating negligible risk of bias from missing outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 606 patients were included in the EPO-TBI trial (Figure 1). Consent was withdrawn in three patients; therefore, this analysis included a total of 603 patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Kidney injury outcomes were assessed based on objective KDIGO criteria using standard laboratory creatinine and urine output measurements collected identically in both blinded study groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Serum creatinine was prospectively recorded daily until ICU discharge and urine output during the first 7 days... Stages of AKI according to KDIGO were defined as follows...

domain_judgments.rationale: The AKI sub-study was pre-planned in an established trial protocol with pre-specified endpoints (KDIGO stage AKI and daily creatinine trajectories) analyzed according to a published statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The EPO-AKI sub-study was a pre-planned study and the protocol (a part of the original EPO-AKI protocol) is included in the Supplementary Materials.

overall_summary: The study is a well-conducted, pre-planned secondary analysis of a large, double-blind randomized controlled trial with concealed allocation, nearly complete follow-up, and objective outcome criteria (KDIGO AKI definitions), resulting in a low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is a randomized clinical trial where participants were randomly allocated to either the erythropoietin group or the control group in a 1:1 ratio using a computer-generated random code.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a computer-generated random code and prepared by an independent nurse to conceal allocation, with baseline characteristics well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly allocated to either the EPO or control group in a 1:1 ratio according to simple randomization using a computer-generated random code. ... Medications were prepared by a nurse who knew the patient's group assignment but was not involved in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and surgical/investigator teams were blinded, interventions were administered identically under anesthesia, and analysis followed intention-to-treat without deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The control group received an equal volume of normal saline at the same time point. Medications were prepared by a nurse who knew the patient's group assignment but was not involved in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 98 randomized patients completed the study and had complete data available for the primary outcome analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of ninety-eight patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 49) or normal saline (n = 49), and no patient was dropped out after group allocation (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Acute kidney injury was assessed using standard objective laboratory criteria (AKIN) measured identically across groups by blinded personnel.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint of interest was incidence of AKI, which was diagnosed according to the Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN) criteria (absolute increase in the sCr concentration ≥0.3 mg/dL from baseline or ≥50% increase in the sCr concentration within 48 hours after operation)

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01758861/NCT0178861), and all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed and reported according to the defined protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This single-site trial was conducted at Yonsei University Health System, Seoul, Korea (Clinical-Trials.gov NCT0178861). ... The primary endpoint of interest was incidence of AKI, which was diagnosed according to the Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN) criteria

overall_summary: The study was a rigorously conducted double-blind randomized controlled trial with adequate sequence generation and allocation concealment, zero attrition, objective laboratory-based outcome assessment, and adherence to a pre-registered analysis plan. All five RoB 2 domains were assessed as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is an exploratory post hoc analysis of data from a randomized controlled trial (Epo-ACR-02) in which eligible patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to an erythropoietin intervention group or a control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were randomized 1:1 with site stratification, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups consistent with proper random allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After being screened for eligibility, patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or to the control group. Intervention assignments were stratified by site.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label, and post-randomization exclusions (patients who died within 24 hours and those with CKD) along with post hoc subgroup selection may deviate from a strict intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among patients included in the Epo-ACR-02 trial, those with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and those who died within the first 24 h after ICU admission were excluded from the present analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Day 2 primary outcome data were available for nearly all included participants (72/74 in the Epo group and 83/88 in the control group), with very minimal missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At Day 2, 52.8% of the patients (38/72) in the intervention group had an AKI, as compared with 54.4% of the patients (46/83) in the control group (P ¼ 0.74).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is based on objective laboratory measurements (serum creatinine) and standardized clinical criteria (urine output and KDIGO definitions), making measurement bias unlikely despite the open-label design.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint of the study was the presence of AKI at Day 2... We used Stages 2 and 3 of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria to define AKI.

domain_judgments.rationale: This was an exploratory post hoc analysis of a subgroup from a single center not pre-specified in the original RCT protocol, raising some concerns for selection of the reported analyses and outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study is a post hoc analysis of the multicentre, single-blind, randomized controlled trial Epo-ACR-02... We therefore aimed to explore, post hoc, in a subgroup of the Epo-ACR-02 trial population, whether there are any renoprotective effects of Epo therapy on patients with resuscitated CA.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as 'some concerns' driven by Domain 2 (post-randomization exclusions of early deaths and non-ITT approach) and Domain 5 (unplanned post hoc subgroup analysis of a single participating center without a pre-registered analysis plan for these specific renal endpoints).

design_rationale: The study is described as a double-blind, randomized controlled trial where participants were assigned to erythropoietin or control groups using computer-generated randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was computer-generated and implemented by an independent investigator who prepared the solutions, ensuring allocation concealment, with baseline characteristics balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent investigator performed computer-generated randomization, enrolled patients, and assigned patients to the erythropoietin group or the control group. He also prepared all drug solutions and provided them to the anesthesia practitioner.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind administration was maintained with identical placebo solution, and no significant deviations from intended intervention protocols were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The anesthetic administrator, surgeons, patients, outcome assessors, and data analysts were all blinded to patient allocations throughout the entire study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 6 of 66 enrolled patients were excluded prior to analysis as detailed in the CONSORT flow diagram, and outcome data were complete for 60 participants (31 vs 29) without differential attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 66 patients enrolled, 60 patients were included in the final analysis (Fig 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures were objective biochemical definitions (serum creatinine, RIFLE criteria) and assessors were blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the incidence of AKI according to the RIFLE criteria... The anesthetic administrator, surgeons, patients, outcome assessors, and data analysts were all blinded to patient allocations throughout the entire study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary renal endpoints were clearly pre-specified and reported transparently according to standard clinical criteria without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was incidence of AKI defined according to the RIFLE criteria during the first 7 postoperative days.

overall_summary: The randomized trial used rigorous computer-generated allocation concealment, effective blinding of participants and personnel, had minimal and balanced missing data, used objective diagnostic criteria for AKI, and adhered to pre-specified outcome reporting, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is an ancillary analysis of the PENUT trial, a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial where neonates were randomly assigned 1:1 to recombinant erythropoietin or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The randomized trial used a stratified 1:1 allocation sequence, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between study groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization allocation was 1:1, with patients stratified by gestational age category, multiple births, and study site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, caregivers, and study personnel were blinded to intervention assignment in this double-blind placebo-controlled trial, with no evidence of non-protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study personnel and families were still blinded to randomization groups at the follow-up visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial proportions of surviving participants had missing long-term kidney outcome data (only 49.7% vs 56.8% had BP measured, and fewer had laboratory specimens), with evidence of differential missingness by sex and prior treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Urine, blood, and blood pressure measurements were not a mandatory part of the primary protocol but were encouraged by site personnel to families... Of the 383 subjects who received rhEPO and returned for a follow-up visit, 123 of 383 (32.1%) had both blood and urine collected... 233 of 383 (60.8%) had blood pressure measured... We also acknowledge that a large number of patients did not have kidney-related metrics measured at the 2-year cGA time point.

domain_judgments.rationale: Objective laboratory markers and standardized manual blood pressure measurements were performed by trained staff who remained blinded to intervention status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study personnel and families were still blinded to randomization groups at the follow-up visit... Standardization of procedures and personnel training was done across all sites.

domain_judgments.rationale: This was an ancillary study with multiple defined cutoffs and analytic choices (such as analyzing the lowest recorded BP measurement and selecting the 90th percentile threshold for regression models), introducing some risk of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For purposes of analysis in the regression models, we focus only on the 90th percentile values... We performed a sensitivity analysis to determine whether an alternative approach to reporting blood pressure (BP) (using the average, instead of the lowest BP) would have led to differences in treatment effect.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial missing outcome data for the 22- to 26-month follow-up kidney measures, where over 40% of children lacked blood pressure data and more than half lacked blood or urine collections, accompanied by differential loss to follow-up between arms.

design_rationale: The study explicitly describes random allocation using a computer application to generate randomization tables with concealed allocation sequences.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated by computer software and concealed until enrollment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A custom simple application running in Windows XP (Microsoft Corp, Redmond, WA) was used to ob tain randomization tables, and the next value of the table was kept secret un til a suitable patient was enrolled.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although patients and ward staff were unblinded (open-label/single-blind), transfusion was dictated by standard hospital protocol/triggers and an intention-to-treat approach was followed without reported protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients, nurses, and ward physician knew whether HRE was being administered or not, but the investigators did not, nor did they have any chance to influence the clinical decision as to whether or not to give allo genic blood, thus fulfilling the conditions for a single-blinded study

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were recorded and analyzed for all 320 randomized patients with no apparent loss to follow-up for the primary in-hospital outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the remaining 320 patients, 158 were allocated to HRE administration and all received the intended treatment; 162 were allocated to the control group. Two patients in the HRE group and 1 patient in the control group were converted to on-pump revascularization. These patients were considered as intention-to-treat and were therefore included in the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were laboratory-measured hemoglobin and recorded blood transfusions based on standardized objective clinical criteria with investigators blinded to group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Transfusion need was triggered by Hb levels less than 8.0 g/dL, and the same criteria were applied to both groups. Hb values were automatically collected by the central laboratory computer on the day of admission, on the day of surgery, and on postoperative day 4.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan, leaving some concerns regarding potential selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was the need for allogenic transfusion. The sec ondary end point was the Hb value on postoperative day 4.

overall_summary: The trial was well-conducted with computer-generated randomization, allocation concealment, objective outcome measures, and intention-to-treat analysis. However, the lack of a publicly available pre-registered trial protocol leads to an overall rating of some concerns for selection of the reported result.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where patients were randomized using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence generation was computer-generated, centralized by the data coordinating center ensuring allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics between groups were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was stratified by site and entailed use of computer-generated random numbers (FIGURE 1). ... Randomization and data analysis were done by the data coordinating center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind study design with identical-appearing placebo administered in standard fashion, with analysis performed on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study drug (40000 units of rHuEPO [Procrit; Ortho Biotech Products, LP, Bridgewater, NJ] ) or a placebo identical in appearance was administered by subcutaneous injection on ICU day 3 and continued once weekly for patients who remained in the hospital... Analysis of outcomes was on an intent-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data on RBC transfusion and mortality were available for almost all participants (only minimal loss to follow-up: 4 in placebo, 5 in rHuEPO per Figure 1), and sensitivity analyses showed robust results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were followed up for 28 days, unless death occurred earlier. Analysis of outcomes was on an intent-to-treat basis. Patients not receiving transfusion at the time of study withdrawal or lost to follow-up were considered not transfused for this analysis. In addition, a second analysis was done in which all patients withdrawn or lost to follow-up were considered transfused.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome is objectively documented blood transfusion and laboratory values, assessed identically between groups by clinicians blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy end point was transfusion independence, assessed by comparing the percentage of patients in each treatment group who received any RBC transfusion between study days 1 and 28... Transfusion indication, pretransfusion hemoglobin level, and pretransfusion hematocrit concentration were recorded for each RBC transfusion.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary efficacy end points were pre-specified and all reported in accordance with the pre-planned protocol analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy end point was transfusion independence, assessed by comparing the percentage of patients in each treatment group who received any RBC transfusion between study days 1 and 28. Secondary efficacy end points identified prospectively were cumulative RBC units transfused per patient through study day 28; cumulative mortality through study day 28; change in hemoglobin from baseline; and time to first transfusion or death.

overall_summary: This was a rigorous, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled multicenter trial with centralized allocation, robust blinding, minimal loss to follow-up, and objective, pre-specified outcomes analyzed by intention to treat, presenting low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with participants allocated using a predefined computer-generated randomization sequence with permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used a computer-generated sequence stratified by center, concealment was maintained through preparation of identical syringes by pharmacy, and baseline differences were minor and consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible patients were allocated to EPO or placebo (normal saline) groups in a 1:1 ratio, using a predefined computer-generated randomization sequence with permuted blocks stratified on center. Concealment was by pharmacist; pairs of identical 5-ml syringes containing EPO (50 000 U in 3 ml) or normal saline were prepared and stored.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of patients, medical staff, and investigators was maintained using identical placebo syringes, and an intention-to-treat analysis was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients, all medical staff, and investigators were masked to treatment... The primary outcome and safety endpoints were evaluated in the ITT population. ITT patients were those with an increased GGT - AP index who had been randomized. As all randomized patients had received at least one dose of the study medication; the ITT and safety populations were identical.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for all 162 randomized patients in the ITT analysis, with only 1 patient withdrawing consent prior to data recording out of 163 randomized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome and safety endpoints were evaluated in the ITT population. ITT patients were those with an increased GGT - AP index who had been randomized. (Table 3 ITT: Placebo n=78, EPO n=84; one patient withdrew consent for recording data prior to intervention cohort count of 162).

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome was objective laboratory measurements of plasma creatinine evaluated blindly and identically across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The prospectively defined primary outcome was the RAVC, defined as the average pCr (pC) increase from baseline (pC - pCb) as a percentage of baseline creatinine (pCb)... Urine GGT, AP and creatinine, and pCr were assayed immediately... Patients, all medical staff, and investigators were masked to treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the primary outcome and secondary outcomes were defined prior to unmasking, and results are reported in accordance with the pre-specified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the multiregional ethics committee of New Zealand (MEC/050020029) and registered under the Australian Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN012606000058572; http://www.actr.org.au)... The prospectively defined primary outcome was the RAVC... Secondary outcomes, defined before unmasking included RIFLE... and AKIN...

overall_summary: This trial was judged to be at low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains due to sound randomization with pharmacy concealment, double blinding, complete outcome reporting for the intention-to-treat population, objective laboratory outcome measurements, and prospective trial registration.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, randomized controlled trial where eligible patients were allocated to EPO or control using permuted block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization used permuted blocks with central allocation and blinding, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible patients were allocated to EPO (Recormon, Roche, epoetin beta) plus standard preventive protocol treatment (normal saline + NAC) or standard preventive protocol only in a 1:1 ratio, using a permuted block randomization. The patients and the interventional cardiologist were blinded to treatment assignment. ... The validity of our study is strengthened by use of double blinding and central randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and procedural cardiologists were blinded, a matching saline control bolus was used, background care was standardized, and all randomized patients were analyzed in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients and the interventional cardiologist were blinded to treatment assignment. Standard preventive protocol included NAC ... In addition, patients in the EPO group received 50 000 U of EPO intravenously over approximately 2 min followed by 2 mL of saline 30 min before the CA. Patients in the control group received a bolus of saline only.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data for the primary outcome of contrast-induced nephropathy by serum creatinine were available for all 138 randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomized 138 patients to receive EPO (n = 72) or saline (n = 66). ... When defined as an increase in SCr level, compared to baseline value, of at least 0.5 mg/dL during first 2 days after exposure to contrast media, CIN occurred in 12 of the 138 patients (8.7%).

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome was measured via objective laboratory assays of serum creatinine at prespecified standardized time points, with blinding of participants and clinicians.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the incidence of CIN after CA, defined as an increase in SCr level, compared to baseline value, of at least 0.5 mg/dL during the first 2 days after exposure to contrast media. ... SCr post CA was measured at 24 and 48 h post-procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov and reported the prespecified primary outcome and analyses in full.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (www. clinicaltrial.gov), No. NCT01364402. ... The primary endpoint was the incidence of CIN after CA, defined as an increase in SCr level, compared to baseline value, of at least 0.5 mg/dL during the first 2 days after exposure to contrast media.

overall_summary: The study is judged to be at low risk of bias across all five domains due to proper central block randomization, participant and procedural blinding, complete follow-up for the primary outcome, objective laboratory outcome measurement, and reporting consistent with the prospective trial registry.

design_rationale: The study is described as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group trial where patients were allocated to treatment groups using a computer-generated randomization code.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central registration with computer-generated randomization ensured an adequate random sequence generation and concealed allocation, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were registered centrally, stratified by center, and randomized before scheduled operation to receive either Epoetin alfa or placebo on the basis of a computer-generated randomization code.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and placebo-controlled, with both evaluable and intention-to-treat analyses conducted with concordant results, and no deviations from intended interventions were reported that would bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Identity of study medication was blinded, but the volume administered was not blinded to the investigators... Investigators were provided labeled study medication and dosing supplies for each patient. Study medications were administered by study personnel or visiting nurses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Transfusion outcomes were available for almost all patients who underwent surgery (173/173 undergoing CABG; 9 patients total did not undergo CABG), and results were confirmed in ITT analyses without evidence of bias from missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study enrolled 182 patients (63 = 300 IU/kg Epoetin alfa, 63 = 150 IU/kg Epoetin alfa, and 56 = placebo). Of those, 171 (94.0%...) were evaluable for efficacy... Intent-to-treat patients: 20 (33%) (n = 60), 17 (28%) (n = 61), 25 (48%) (n = 52).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of transfusion was objective, governed by a defined transfusion trigger protocol, and investigators and participants were blinded to the treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The investigators used a policy not to transfuse patients with an HCT value greater than 24% after CABG unless clinically indicated... The number of units of allogeneic blood (ie, whole blood and packed RBCs) transfused was recorded daily starting on the day of operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary efficacy variables and planned statistical methods were clearly specified and reported according to the predefined analysis plan without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy variable was the proportion of patients given a transfusion. The number of allogeneic units of RBCs transfused and the changes in Hb, HCT, and reticulocyte count from baseline to preoperative, preoperative to postoperative day 1, and postoperative day 1 to discharge were analyzed as secondary efficacy variables.

overall_summary: This multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial has a low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains, including adequate centralized randomization, successful blinding of participants and providers, low attrition with concordant ITT analyses, standardized outcome measurement, and pre-specified reporting.

design_rationale: The study explicitly describes randomized allocation using a permuted block randomization scheme with 1:1 allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation and allocation concealment were appropriately implemented, and baseline characteristics between groups were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A permuted block randomization scheme with 1:1 allocation was used to keep the group sizes equal. Randomization was performed by a study coordinator immediately after consent was obtained but group assignments were not disclosed to the investigators until the study was complete.

domain_judgments.rationale: Treating clinical staff were blinded to group assignment, protocol adherence was maintained under standard surgical conditions, and analysis was performed on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All investigators, surgeons, anesthesiologists, perfusionists, and intensive care unit physicians responsible for the administration of blood products or involved in the evaluation of outcomes were blinded with respect to group assignment thereby creating a single-blinded study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were complete for all 600 enrolled patients across both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Sixteen patients died in the hospital (5.3%), and three more patients died during rehabilitation (1%) outside our facility. None of the survivors were lost to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of transfusion was assessed according to a strict predefined Hb trigger (8.0 g/dL) by healthcare providers blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A trigger Hb level of 8.0 g/dL was strictly observed as threshold for transfusions allowing no discretion to physicians. ... All investigators, surgeons, anesthesiologists, perfusionists, and intensive care unit physicians responsible for the administration of blood products or involved in the evaluation of outcomes were blinded with respect to group assignment thereby creating a single-blinded study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01265680) and all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes were reported in accordance with the protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study adhered to the CONSORT principles and patients followed the CONSORT 2005 Flow Chart (Fig. 1) and was registered at Clinicaltrials.gov with the Clinical Trial Registration Number NCT01265680.

overall_summary: The trial demonstrated low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains due to sound permuted block randomization with allocation concealment, blinding of clinical caretakers and outcome assessors, standardized strict transfusion triggers, complete follow-up, and prospective trial registration.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with participants allocated 1:1 using a computer-generated randomization schema.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated via a computer schema, stratified, concealed by an independent technician, and baseline differences were largely balanced with the minor baseline hemoglobin imbalance appropriately adjusted for.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were assigned to receive EPO (+iron) or placebo using a computer-generated randomisation schema in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by planned route (transfemoral [TF] vs. transapical [TA]/transaortic [TAO]). Randomisation was performed by a technician who was not otherwise involved in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients, investigators, and outcome assessors were blinded using placebos and draped tubing, and there were no substantial deviations from intended interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intravenous tubing used for administering the iron (or placebo) was covered with a drape to guarantee that the patient could not see the infusion solution. Both the EPO (+iron sucrose) and placebo were administered by a nurse not involved in the screening, randomisation or assessing of patient outcomes. The investigator was not present during the infusion to ensure the blindness of treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: All patients who underwent the procedure completed 30-day follow-up with no loss to follow-up, and transfusion data were verified with the central blood bank.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were followed for 30 days and no patients were lost at follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objectively measured using standardized guideline triggers and confirmed by an independent, blinded blood bank.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment assignments were concealed from the investigators gathering data and assessing outcome and safety events until the study was complete. All data were prospectively collected. Data regarding RC transfusions were further confirmed using the data from the local blood bank (Héma-Québec, Canada), which was blinded regarding treatment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively on ClinicalTrials.gov and reported all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes according to the predefined analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02390102

overall_summary: The trial was rigorously conducted with computer-generated randomized allocation, robust blinding of participants, caregivers, and outcome assessors, complete follow-up confirmed with independent blood bank records, and prespecified reporting.
